title: Dungeon Game
description: Brute force to optimized: forward path search combined with a health search versus a backward-filled 2D DP grid.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: A knight starts at the top-left of a dungeon grid (each cell either damages or heals) and must reach the bottom-right (moving only right or down) to rescue a princess. The knight's health must never drop to 0 or below at any point along the path. Return the minimum initial health needed to guarantee survival.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","dungeon grid of integers (negative for damage, positive for healing)"],["Output","Minimum starting health to survive the path to the bottom-right"],["Key Insight","Working BACKWARD from the destination, the health needed entering a room depends on the health needed entering whichever NEXT room is chosen"],["Constraints","Up to 200 by 200 grid"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Minimum resource needed to survive a path, where the requirement depends on FUTURE steps\"","A backward DP: since the required health at any point depends on what comes AFTER it (not before), fill the DP grid starting from the destination and working back to the start"]]}

blocks.text: Filling this DP grid FORWARD (from the start) does not work cleanly, since the minimum health needed at the START depends on the ENTIRE path chosen, which is not yet known. Instead, define dp[i][j] as the MINIMUM health needed just BEFORE entering room (i, j) in order to survive from there all the way to the destination. This is computed BACKWARD, starting from the destination (where dp is trivially 1, needing at least 1 health point remaining after that room's effect) and working back toward the start.

blocks.title: Analogy: Figuring Out How Much Fuel You Needed at the START, by Reasoning Backward From the Destination
blocks.text: Picture figuring out the minimum fuel needed at the START of a road trip with segments that consume or refill fuel, where the tank must never run empty. This is naturally figured out by reasoning BACKWARD from the destination: how much fuel is needed just before the LAST segment, then just before the segment before that, and so on back to the very beginning.

blocks.caption: Working backward from the destination, health needed entering a room depends on health needed entering the next room

blocks.text: Minimum initial health = 7 (the path right, right, down, down needs exactly this much to never drop to 0 or below).
Minimum initial health = 1 (a single room with no effect still requires at least 1 health point).

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Define dp[i][j] as the minimum health needed just BEFORE stepping into room (i, j), so that health remains at least 1 after this room's effect and for the entire rest of the journey.

Observation 2: At the destination (bottom-right room), the knight needs at least 1 health point AFTER that room's effect, so the health needed BEFORE entering it is max(1, 1 - dungeon[destination]).

Observation 3: For any other room, the knight will move to WHICHEVER of the room below or the room to the right requires LESS health beforehand (the cheaper of the two options), so dp[i][j] = max(1, min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1]) - dungeon[i][j]).

Observation 4: Padding the DP grid with a virtual extra row and column set to infinity (except exactly one artificial entry set to 1) cleanly handles the destination's base case using the SAME general formula, without needing special-cased boundary logic.
This leads to a 2D DP grid filled BACKWARD from the destination, where each cell's required health depends on the cheaper of its two possible next rooms.

Conceptually, try every possible path FORWARD from the start, tracking current health along the way, but this cannot easily determine the OPTIMAL starting health without first knowing which path will ultimately be chosen.

codes.python:
# Conceptually: try every path from top-left to bottom-right directly,
# simulating health changes forward and checking if a given starting
# health survives that specific path, then binary search or trial over
# possible starting health values across ALL paths. Correct in principle,
# but extremely inefficient, needing to explore an exponential number of
# paths combined with a search over starting health values.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Trying every path forward directly mirrors how the knight actually experiences the journey.

This cannot cleanly determine the OPTIMAL starting health without effectively searching over both all paths AND all possible starting health values, prohibitively expensive; working backward from the destination avoids this entirely.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: exponential, combining an exhaustive path search with a starting-health search.
Space: O(m+n) per path.
Limitation: a backward-filled 2D DP grid directly computes the minimum required health at every position in a single O(m times n) pass.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: Build a (m+1) by (n+1) DP grid, initialized to infinity, with dp[m][n-1] = 1 and dp[m-1][n] = 1 (virtual entries representing "just past the destination", both needing at least 1 health point remaining). Fill the grid from the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner backward to the TOP-LEFT: for each cell (i, j), compute dp[i][j] = max(1, min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1]) - dungeon[i][j]). The final answer is dp[0][0].
Fill a 2D DP grid backward from the destination, each cell depending on the cheaper of the room below or the room to the right.

codes.python:
def calculate_minimum_hp(dungeon):
    m, n = len(dungeon), len(dungeon[0])
    dp = [[float('inf')] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]
    dp[m][n - 1] = 1                                       # virtual: just past the destination
    dp[m - 1][n] = 1
    for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):                          # fill BACKWARD from the destination
        for j in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            need = min(dp[i + 1][j], dp[i][j + 1]) - dungeon[i][j]
            dp[i][j] = max(1, need)                            # health can never drop below 1
    return dp[0][0]

blocks.text: Filling the grid BACKWARD from the destination correctly reflects that the required health at any position genuinely depends on what happens AFTER it, not before; choosing the CHEAPER of the two possible next rooms at each step correctly models the knight taking whichever path minimizes the required starting health, and clamping every value to at least 1 correctly enforces that health can never drop to 0 or below at any point along the journey.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(m times n).
Space: O(m times n), reducible to O(n) using a rolling row.

blocks.text: Dungeon Game is the standout example of "when forward DP does not work because the requirement depends on the future, fill the DP grid backward from the destination instead".

items: Attempting to fill the DP grid forward from the start, which cannot correctly determine minimum health without first knowing the entire future path.
Forgetting to clamp every dp value to at least 1, incorrectly allowing a computed "required health" of 0 or negative, which would violate the survive-at-all-times constraint.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","Expected Behavior"],"rows":[["A single room with a very large healing value","The minimum starting health is still at least 1, regardless of how much healing is available."],["A path where every room only deals damage","The minimum starting health equals 1 plus the total damage along the best (least damaging) path."]]}

blocks.text: Explicitly stating "fill the DP grid backward, since the required health depends on the future, not the past" is the single most important insight to communicate for this problem.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "minimum resource needed to survive a path, where the requirement depends on future steps", think: fill the DP grid backward from the destination.

items: How would you also reconstruct the actual optimal path achieving this minimum starting health?
Minimum Path Sum and Unique Paths, both closely related grid DP problems, though solvable forward since they lack this future-dependent twist.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The forward-search-combined-with-health-search approach is prohibitively expensive; the backward-filled 2D DP grid costs O(m times n), the standard efficient and elegant solution.

items: Pattern: backward-filled 2D dynamic programming, starting from the destination.
Core Idea: dp[i][j] = max(1, min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1]) - dungeon[i][j]), since required health depends on the future path.
Time: exponential for the forward-search approach, O(m times n) for the backward DP.
Space: O(m+n) per path for the forward approach, O(m times n) (reducible to O(n)) for the backward DP.
Most Important Observation: when a requirement depends on the future, fill the DP grid backward from the destination instead of forward from the start.
Interview Difficulty: a hard, conceptually tricky grid DP problem.
One line memory trick: work backward; health never drops below 1.
